newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork belly futures expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork belly futures expected lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent per lb lower while pork bellies were called 0.200 to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Although hog futures closed technically strong Thursday, analysts look for early pressure Friday. Thursday's gains were overdone in light of the weaker than expected cash pork complex and lower cash hog indications early, they said.

Packer slaughter margins are already deep in the red and the weakness in pork products will encourage them to lower bids, especially with continued rainy weather boosting hog runs in the Midwest, they said.

Pork belly futures were called lower following a break in cash belly prices and the weak futures close Thursday. Bellies ended lower despite sharply higher hog futures with some pressure also coming from long hog/short belly spreading, analyts said.

Reduced domestic demand for bellies will likely keep futures pressured despite the recent light pace of storings. There are very few bellies, if any, being put into storage due to light hog slaughter and recent export business, they added.
